sources.entry: RecipeSage - A recipe keeper, meal plan organizer, and shopping list manager that can import recipes directly from any URL. (Demo) AGPL-3.0 Nodejs

summary.one_liner: RecipeSage is a self-hostable recipe keeper with meal planning, shared shopping lists, and recipe import from URLs, images, PDFs, and other formats.
summary.what_it_does: It stores and searches a personal recipe collection, with full-text search that tolerates misspellings and tags for filtering. Recipes can be imported from any URL, image, PDF, or text, as well as from several recipe apps, notes apps, JSON-LD, and CSV. A drag-and-drop meal planner lets users schedule meals and print the plan. Shopping lists are automatically categorized, and adding recipes merges similar items. Recipes can be scaled and converted between metric and imperial units, and nutrition data can be tracked per serving. The app is a Progressive Web App that the README says works offline and syncs across devices. Recipes, meal plans, and shopping lists can be shared with family or friends, and exports go to PDF, JSON-LD, or text.
use_cases: Organize and search a personal recipe collection
Import recipes from a website URL
Generate a categorized shared shopping list from recipes
Migrate recipes from other recipe apps
how_to_run: Preferred selfhosting: use the preconfigured docker compose files in the separate selfhost repository linked from the README (link not given in the text)
For development: install Docker and Node, clone the repo, and create a .env file from example.env
Run corepack enable, then pnpm install at the repo root
Start containers with docker compose up -d
Run database migrations: docker compose exec backend pnpm exec prisma migrate dev
notable: Dual-licensed: AGPL-3.0 for non-commercial use, commercial use requires a paid license from the author
Built-in AI cooking assistant for substitutions, techniques, and conversions
Imports from many recipe managers and notes apps, including Paprika, Evernote, Notion, and Obsidian
Translations managed through a Weblate instance
caveats: Commercial use requires a separate license with pricing based on usage
The author does not accept AI-assisted code contributions
Self-hosting config is in a separate repo; the README warns that custom setups may run into complications
The AI assistant and some dependent features need real API keys in the .env file
